subject: Nanotechnology
title: Liposomes: The First Nano Drug Carrier
description: A quick, practical guide to Liposomes: The First Nano Drug Carrier.

hook.text: In 1995, Doxil became the first FDA-approved nano drug — doxorubicin wrapped in a tiny fat bubble.

buildup.text: Liposomes are hollow spheres made of lipid bilayers — the same material that forms cell membranes.

discovery.text: Drugs loaded inside liposomes are shielded from degradation and delivered more gently to tissues.

twist.text: Doxil reduced heart toxicity of doxorubicin dramatically — but did not improve overall cancer survival rates.

climax.text: Despite mixed results, liposomes paved the way — COVID mRNA vaccines use lipid nanoparticles descended from them.

punchline.text: A fat bubble carrying medicine launched the nanomedicine era.

quiz.question: What are liposomes made of?
options: Lipid bilayers that form hollow spheres
